old_description: We offer various spectrometers, monochromators, light sources, integrating spheres, detectors,
about:
Spectral Products is headquartered in Putnam, Connecticut, with additional offices in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Seoul, South Korea. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It operates as a manufacturer of optical instrumentation.

The company designs and builds spectrometers, monochromators, light sources, integrating spheres, detectors, fiber-optic accessories, adapters, and filter wheels. Its product lines include the SM series of miniature spectrometers—such as the SM301/SM301-EX PbS(e) array spectrometer covering 1.0–3.0 µm and the TE-cooled SM304 InGaAs array spectrometer—the CM110 compact 1/8-meter monochromator with customizable slits, and the ASBN-W high-power tungsten-halogen light source assemblies featuring fused-silica lenses and UV-protected aluminum mirrors. An Optics Division also supplies optical coatings and coated optics for high-energy applications.

Spectral Products serves industrial, laboratory, research, and scientific markets, working directly with system designers and end users. The company maintains international representatives in Europe, Asia, and Australia.

The firm attributes its differentiation to an innovative direct-drive technique introduced more than a decade ago, which it says revolutionized computer-based spectrometers and monochromators by delivering high performance at lower cost. Its SM miniature spectrometers are marketed as combining essential features and optimal performance in a small footprint.

name: Sprague Woodworking Co
old_description: Quality Craftsmanship and Superior Personal Service since 1979
about:
Sprague Woodworking Co. has been based in Harvard, Massachusetts since 1979. The family-owned and operated shop was founded on a commitment to quality craftsmanship and personal service, and it remains a family-run business today.

The company specializes in custom solid wood countertops, including butcher block and plank styles, as well as shelves, desktops, and tabletops. Each piece is handcrafted from an extensive inventory of domestic hardwoods, with the option to source reclaimed or exotic species. Sprague Woodworking also provides professional templating and installation services within a 120-mile radius of its shop, along with a range of finish options to suit any design.

Its work appears in residential projects throughout New England, from Boston brownstones to coastal retreats. The shop serves homeowners, builders, and designers seeking one-of-a-kind wood surfaces for kitchens, bathrooms, and commercial spaces.

The company emphasizes unmatched personal service from initial consultation through installation, a principle that has guided its operation since its founding.

about:
Square Nail Chicago is based in Chicago, Illinois. The company was founded by brothers Mike and Dan Wynne, both Chicago natives, who began by sourcing wood from knocked-down factories and abandoned barns across the region.

The operation focuses on turning reclaimed lumber — including walnut, white elm, red elm, oak, and pine — into finished pieces that showcase the wood's natural knots, warping, and nail holes. In addition to wood, the workshop incorporates found metal and glass to add layers of history and texture. The company does not disclose its facility size, employee count, or production volumes.

Square Nail Chicago caters to clients looking for one-of-a-kind furniture and architectural accents made from salvaged materials, though specific industry sectors or customer profiles are not publicly listed. The founders' motivation, as described in company materials, is to highlight the appreciated beauty and personality that emerges from materials others might discard, giving new life to wood, metal, and glass with a storied past.

name: Stack Electronics
old_description: Established since 1983, one of the longest industry tenures within global independent distribution, STACK ELECTRONICS is recognized as a world leader in the distribution of electronic components & computer products.
about:
Stack Electronics, based in Rolling Hills Estates, California, has operated as an independent distributor of electronic components and computer products since its founding in 1983. The company has built a global footprint over four decades, positioning itself as a long-tenured player in the distribution sector.

The firm supplies a broad range of electronic components and offers value-added services including scheduled orders, tape-and-reeling, kitting, excess-materials management and asset recovery, market intelligence, and rigorous quality-control programs. Its quality system is certified to AS9120B with ISO 9001:2015 and follows IDEA-QMS-9090 incoming-inspection standards, supported by a photo-archive traceability system and partnerships with accredited test laboratories.

Stack serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), original design manufacturers (ODMs), contract manufacturers (CMs), and Tier 1 suppliers across industries that require high-reliability electronic components, including aerospace and defense applications implied by its AS9120B certification.

The company emphasizes a solutions-oriented approach, citing on-time delivery of critical items, strategic cost savings, strict supplier vetting, and continuous improvement tracked through supplier performance metrics as key differentiators.

name: Staco Systems
old_description: Lighted pushbutton and avionic switches, keyboards, HMI panels for aerospace/defense
about:
Staco Systems was founded in 1958 in Costa Mesa, California, originally operating as Staco Switch. The company began by supplying lighted pushbutton display switches to the aviation and defense firms clustered in Southern California, with its first Series 30 switch flying on a Fokker F-27 in 1960. Today the headquarters is in Irvine, California, and the firm maintains sales representatives in more than 35 countries.

The product line has expanded from those early switches to include rugged keyboards and keypads, electronic controllers, panel assemblies, edge‑lit panels, and complete cockpit control assemblies. Staco emphasizes custom engineering, citing advances in optics, weight reduction, and miniaturization as core technical capabilities. The company serves as a manufacturer of human‑machine interface components, producing both standard and custom solutions for demanding applications.

Staco’s customer base spans military, aerospace, shipboard, ground vehicle, naval, industrial, power‑generation, and flight‑simulation markets. The company references its long‑standing relationships with major aerospace and defense primes, though specific client names are not disclosed. Historical examples include the Fokker F‑27 installation and ongoing supply to military and commercial aviation programs.

Staco attributes its longevity to a commitment to quality and custom problem‑solving, backed by certifications such as AS9100 and MIL‑SPEC. The firm states that its differentiation lies in superior engineering and continual technology development that enable unique custom solutions tailored to customer specifications.

about:
Stanford Manufacturing operates from two facilities totaling over 100,000 square feet in Clemmons, North Carolina. The company traces its molding expertise back more than six decades, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been released.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding, supported by automation and assembly, packaging, labeling, and shipping services. Its capabilities include multi-color molding, decorating and joining technologies, barcode traceability, automated vision inspection with touch probes, and leak detection. Production volumes range from 100 to over 10 million parts annually.

Stanford serves industries including waste bins and totes, aerospace and defense, consumer goods, electrical, industrial products, and agriculture. Long-term customers cited include Battery Watering Technologies (over eight years), Faircloth Machine Shop, Pronet Solutions, and Xtreme Defense Face Shield.

The company emphasizes precision, flexibility, and full-service integration from molding through final shipment. It highlights its ISO 9001 and AS9100D certifications, consolidated logistics, and a workforce recognized by the Triad's Best Places to Work award.

name: Stark Mountain Woodworking Co
old_description: Blending time honored wood craft with the tech of today in the mountains of Vermont since 1993
about:
Stark Mountain Woodworking Co. was founded in 1993 in New Haven, Vermont, a town of about 1,800 people in the state's mountainous region. The business began as a two-person shop and has grown to a team of more than 20 craftspeople operating from a 24,000-square-foot facility.

The company provides full-service custom woodworking, producing cabinetry for homes and offices, furniture, and architectural millwork for institutions such as museums, libraries, and colleges. Each project moves through design collaboration, 2D and 3D shop drawings created with AutoCAD, DataCAD, AlphaCam, and Cabinet Vision, CNC fabrication on three- and five-axis routers, moulding, sanding, edge banding, finishing in a dedicated spray booth, and final assembly and installation. A bandsaw mill and vacuum kiln give the shop control over lumber from tree to finished product, and a full metal shop handles architectural finishes in stainless steel and bronze.

Clients include architects, interior designers, general contractors, and homeowners. Notable project types range from residential and commercial interiors to institutional work for colleges, libraries, and museums.

Stark Mountain has been FSC-certified since 2001 and sources a large percentage of its lumber within a 30-mile radius. The facility runs on roughly 60 percent solar power, with a 54 kW hillside array and a 34 kW rooftop array, and is heated by a pelletizer that converts shop sawdust into fuel. A bike-to-work program has logged over 145,000 commuter miles since 2006.

name: Steadfast Farms
old_description: The New Standard in USDA-inspected Poultry Processing in New England
about:
Steadfast Farms is based in Bethlehem, Connecticut. Founded in 2017 by Jared McCool, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who began farming after his honorable discharge in 2014, the veteran-owned operation started as a continuation of military service, applying principles of discipline and resilience to agriculture.

The company runs Connecticut’s only USDA-inspected poultry slaughter and processing facility, providing fee-for-service processing to more than 180 farms across the Northeast. The plant is certified for USDA Organic slaughter and holds Animal Welfare Approved verification, enabling interstate sales of processed birds. In addition to contract processing, Steadfast Farms raises its own pasture-raised poultry—quail, chicken, turkey, pheasant, and chukar partridge—using regenerative farming practices. The facility also offers parting, grinding, sausage making, and stock production.

Steadfast Farms serves two primary customer groups: independent poultry farmers who need USDA-inspected processing to bring birds to market, and wholesale buyers such as restaurants, retailers, and food-service distributors. The company also works with game-bird clubs and other B2B farm partners throughout the region.

McCool has stated that the business was founded to extend his service to the domestic community, emphasizing regenerative land stewardship, humane animal handling, and transparent production. The company’s stated values—Rooted in Resilience, Integrity in Every Bite, Delivering the Promise, Pioneer Partner Empower—reflect a commitment to consistent quality and ethical farming from hatch to harvest.
